$about: The one source of the AhaSlides colour and background rules. generate.mjs renders the human page (foundations/brand-colour-rules.html), the agent feeds (colour-rules.agent.json, colour-rules.md) and the Background library page from this file; build-splash.mjs reads splash for its geometry and colours; the anti-slop surfaces colour and background and guidelines/background.json cite rules here by id. Edit a rule here and nowhere else. Text markup: **bold**, `code`, [[#HEX]] is a click-to-copy code with a swatch, [[#HEX|plain]] one without, ((small print)), [label](href), and a line break is a new line. A rule with no environment takes its section's; a section with none takes the file's. origin names where a rule came from when it was not on the rules page of 8 October 2026.
title: AhaSlides visual identity: colour rules
lede: These rules replace the colour section of the current brand guidelines. Everything not mentioned here (the font, spacing, components, icons) stays as it is in the design system.
glance: Vivid Pink (`#E70E68`) is the one primary colour. Purple is the logo only, plus one small playful touch on white.
Page backgrounds are white, and the first screen is white. Two coloured sections never sit next to each other, and at most two of them are Vivid Pink.
Social, ads, slides, print and video use white or Vivid Pink backgrounds. Nothing else.
Splash backgrounds come in three layouts only: centre, right and minimal.
Pink text is for white only. On Vivid Pink at 5% or on grey, text is black. On Vivid Pink, text is solid white.
No red, yellow, green or blue for status. Use an icon, clear wording and an outline or black fill. One green and one red mark a correct or wrong answer, and nothing else (section 11).
Charts use four colours in order: Vivid Pink, black, Vivid Pink at 30%, light grey.
Illustrations use Vivid Pink tints, Darker Pink, white, the default ink and grey. The 10, 20, 45, 60 and 80% tints never appear in the interface.

blocks.text: The two tints are Vivid Pink with transparency (the last two digits are the alpha). The flat codes in brackets match them on a white page only. Colours are defined in RGB (hex) only; when something goes to print, convert them then. The contrast figures in section 10 are measured on white.

No other colour appears on anything we draw ourselves. Photos and customer content are exempt (see section 9). The one exception is the correct green and wrong red, which mark a correct or wrong answer and nothing else (section 11).

Illustrations may use Vivid Pink at any of these tints, plus Darker Pink, white, the default ink and grey. The 10, 20, 45, 60 and 80% tints are for illustrations only and never appear in the interface. Vivid Pink, its 5% and 30% tints and Darker Pink keep their interface roles in the table above.
Work shipped before 8 October 2026 used the colours below. They are listed only so an older asset can be recognised and its replacement looked up. Never use them in new work.

rows: Radical Purple as a background, button or text colour
Retired outside the logo. Vivid Pink for buttons, white or Vivid Pink for backgrounds
Deep Space Blue as a text or background colour
Black for text; no dark backgrounds. The logo wordmark keeps its own colour

blocks.text: Near matches are not the brand colours either: `#7C3AED`, `#EC4899` and `#14B8A6` are never used.

rules.text: Two versions of the full logo are allowed: the colour logo on white, and the white logo on Vivid Pink.
The logo and its splash icon are unchanged except for one thing: the two hooks that were Radical Pink are now Vivid Pink. The purple hooks and the wordmark stay as they are.
An all-pink logo on a white background is not allowed.
The font is Plus Jakarta Sans, unchanged.
Every product carries the AhaSlides brand: AhaSlides Livelify, AhaSlides Games, AhaSlides Learn, AhaSlides Docs.

Customer and integration logos (Zoom, Claude and others) are shown in one colour: greyscale or Vivid Pink, never in their own brand colours. On a Vivid Pink background they are white. One treatment per row of logos.

Purple appears in the logo. Outside it, purple may be used very sparingly for a dramatic or playful touch: one small decorative element per page, post or slide at most, on white only. It is never used for text people need to read, buttons, links, states, charts or backgrounds, and never in the product app. If unsure, leave it out.

blocks.text: Which rules apply depends on how the page is built. A web page built from full-width sections stacked down the page, such as a landing page, a pricing page, an article, a help article, or a sign-up or upgrade page, follows rules 3.2 to 3.5, whether it sits on the public website or inside the product. A screen of the product app, such as the editor, the dashboard or settings, follows rules 3.6 and 3.7. Every other rule in this section applies to both.

rules.text: The page background is always white.

There are two kinds of coloured section: a **Vivid Pink section** and a **pale pink section** (Vivid Pink at 5%). Pale pink sections and boxes are for web pages built from full-width sections, not for screens of the product app.
Two coloured sections, of either kind, never sit next to each other. A full white section always sits between them; white padding alone does not count.
A page has at most two Vivid Pink sections. Pale pink sections have no limit beyond the rule above.
The first screen is white.

In the product app, light grey is allowed for surfaces that sit inside or beside the white page: cards, sidebars, input fields, table headers and the editor workspace around the slide. Grey is never the background of a whole page or a full-width section.
In the product app, Vivid Pink at 5% is for hover and selected states, plus at most one highlighted panel per screen.
Black backgrounds are allowed in two places only: full-screen presenting, and video or image viewers.
There is no dark mode. People who need a dark screen use their device or browser setting, and our pages must not break under it.

rules.origin: aha-marketing-colors and the design system Background pattern
rules.text: No gradient is used as a background or a fill. The product app has one exception: on an AI feature the gradient sits on the border only, and the fill stays white.
Social posts, ads, slides, print and video use white or Vivid Pink as the background. Nothing else.
No grey or black areas.
Black text and the colour logo on white are fine. That is ink, not background.
No gradients, anywhere. Every fill is solid and flat.
Every video scene sits on white, Vivid Pink or a minimal Splash background (section 5). A background image is never recoloured.

blocks.text: Applied usage on a white or a Vivid Pink surface

A layout is one section of a web page built from full-width sections, one social post, ad, slide or printed piece, or one video scene. Every layout picks one of the two surfaces, then takes the other roles from its column.

rules.text: A tag or label is Vivid Pink with white text on a white surface, and white with Vivid Pink text on a Vivid Pink surface.
The key visual sits in a contrasting card: a white card on a Vivid Pink surface; a pale pink or Vivid Pink card on a white surface.
A photo of a person sits inside a solid Vivid Pink disc or over the Splash hooks.
Vary a deck by alternating white and Vivid Pink surfaces, never by adding a colour.

blocks.text: A splash background is the splash icon from the logo (its four hooks), enlarged so the frame crops it. Figures below are measured from the vector shapes on pages 4 to 10 of the brand PDF.

rules.text: Colour: Vivid Pink at 5% on a white background, Darker Pink on a Vivid Pink background. All hooks are one colour.
Three layouts only: centre, right and minimal.
**Centre splash.** Enlarge the whole icon until it is 4.5 times as wide as the frame's shorter side. Put the point where the four hooks meet at the centre of the frame.

**Right splash.** Enlarge the whole icon until it is 3.0 times as wide as the frame's shorter side. Put the meeting point 79% of the way across (29% of the width right of centre) and vertically centred.

**Minimal splash.** Two copies of the largest hook (the lower-left one in the icon), and nothing else. Size them as if the whole icon were 1.15 times as wide as the frame's longer side, so each hook is 0.73 of the longer side in length. Pin each to its own corner and measure every offset against the longer side. One is turned a quarter-turn anticlockwise and sits in the bottom-left corner, starting 1.35% outside the left edge and rising 19.3% above the bottom edge. The other is turned a quarter-turn clockwise and sits in the top-right corner, ending 1.9% outside the right edge and dropping 19.8% below the top edge. Each is cropped by the frame edge.
Use a splash background on a web page built from full-width sections, a hero area, an empty state, a social post or a slide. Never on a dense app screen such as the editor.

Centre and right zoom against the frame's shorter side, so the splash stays large in very wide or very tall frames and only parts of the curves show. On a 16:9 frame these figures match the PDF to within 0.5%.
Minimal zooms against the frame's longer side, so the two hooks stay in proportion in wide banners and tall stories alike.

columns: Icon width against the frame's shorter side
Where the hooks' meeting point sits
rows: Not set against the shorter side: the icon would be 1.15 times the longer side, so each of the two hooks is 0.73 of the longer side in length

Each hook is pinned to its own corner and every offset is a share of the longer side. Bottom-left hook: 1.35% outside the left edge, rising 19.3% above the bottom edge. Top-right hook: 1.9% outside the right edge, dropping 19.8% below the top edge. This works on any aspect ratio

blocks.text: The [Background library](backgrounds.html) holds the ready-made files: centre, right and minimal at 16:9, 1:1 and 9:16, each on white and on Vivid Pink. For any other size, build the file with the generator on that page.

rules.text: A splash background is built for its exact frame. Never stretch, cover-crop or re-crop one file into another ratio, because that changes the scale these rules fix.

The hooks come from the real icon. Never redraw, reshape or mirror them, turn them outside the two quarter-turns of the minimal layout, recolour a ready-made file, or add a shadow, bevel or 3D effect.
Never place the hooks freehand, as blobs around a subject, as a repeat pattern or in several colours.
A plain white or plain Vivid Pink background is always allowed.
Pick the surface from the message: white is the default and the quieter one; Vivid Pink is for a hero or high-energy moment.
Pick the layout from where the content sits: right when the content is on the left; centre when the content sits in the middle or fills the frame; minimal when the middle must stay clear.
Over the pale pink hooks of a white splash, text is black. Keep a pink headline over the white area, and keep the logo over the plain area.
Export the final image as PNG in sRGB with no transparency, at 1920 by 1080 or larger for 16:9, 1080 by 1080 or larger for a square and 1080 by 1920 or larger for 9:16.

blocks.text: How the generator reads these rules

rules.text: Icon width, for centre and right, is the width of the splash icon's own 802-unit frame.
The meeting point is the centre of the gap the four hooks surround: 414 across and 336 down in the icon's 802 by 788 frame.

Minimal is sized as if the whole icon were 1.15 times as wide as the frame's longer side (icon width is the 802-unit frame, as above), which makes each turned hook 0.73 of the longer side long. Every offset is a share of the longer side, never of the frame's height or width.
The primary button is Vivid Pink with white text. On hover it turns Darker Pink and gains a shadow. No underline.
On a Vivid Pink background the primary button is white with Vivid Pink text.
A destructive action (Delete, Remove) is never the primary button. The safe choice (Cancel, Undo) is.
Text on Vivid Pink is solid white, never see-through white.
Text and links on Vivid Pink at 5% or on grey are black. Pink text there is too faint to pass accessibility.
Pink text is allowed on white only.

blocks.text: Every button and text link, in any medium (an app screen, a web page, an email, an ad or a slide), is the design system [Button](../button/index.html) component. The one exception is the primary button on a Vivid Pink background (rule 6.2): white with a Vivid Pink label, gaining a shadow on hover, with a 2px solid white focus outline 2px away from the button.

rules.text: Red, yellow, green and blue are no longer used for danger, warning, success or information. The correct green and wrong red of section 11 are not status colours: they mark a correct or wrong answer, and nothing else.
Show status with an icon, clear wording and an outline or a black fill.
A rise is plain black with an up arrow. A fall is white on a black pill with a down arrow.
File-type icons are one colour.
Borders and shadows use black, white or a palette colour at any transparency.
Four colours, in this order: Vivid Pink for the main series, black for the second, Vivid Pink at 30%, then light grey ([[#A8A8A8]]).
Aim for four series or fewer. The four colours never increase. Beyond four, repeat them with a dashed line or a pattern and write the label beside each mark.
Anything drawn in Vivid Pink at 30% or light grey carries its value in writing, because both are faint on white.
Give each line its own end shape, so the chart still reads in black and white.
Up and down are shown as in section 7, never with green and red. The one green in a chart is the correct answer's column in a quiz result (section 11); it marks an answer, not a rise.
Presenter and customer content: slides, uploaded images, their own themes.
Photos.
Official AhaSlides themes and palettes are not exempt. They follow these rules.
Our own illustrations, customer and integration logos and file-type icons are not exempt. They follow these rules.
A real product screenshot placed in a design, such as a web page, a social post, an ad, a slide or a video, counts as product or customer content. Never recolour it to fit the palette.

blocks.text: For readers with red-green colour blindness, Vivid Pink and a mid grey look almost the same. That is why the chart greys are limited to black and one light grey, and why the tint is 30% and not 35%.
The target is WCAG 2.1 AA: body text at 4.5 to 1 or more, large text at 3 to 1 or more.
When AhaSlides shows whether an answer is correct or wrong, and only then, it uses one green and one red.
Each tint is the colour at 5% or 30%, flattened on white. In code they are the `--aha-answer-*` tokens on the [Colour](colour.html#answer-colours) page.

rules.text: Green [[#008A05]] and red [[#C7401E]] mark correct and wrong answers, and nothing else: not status, alerts, success or error messages, a rise or a fall, buttons or decoration.
Every green or red mark carries a white tick or cross.
Text is never green or red; it stays the default ink, on a tint too.
Solid colour is only for the tick or cross disc, an answer row's edge and the correct column of a result chart; areas use the 5% or 30% tint.
The pair is fixed: never replaced by deck colours, a theme or Vivid Pink.

changes.text: New section 11, Correct and wrong answers: one green and one red, with 5% and 30% tints, mark a correct or wrong answer and nothing else. Five short rules (11.1 to 11.5) in a collapsed Rules panel. Rules 1.1, 7.1 and 8.5 and the glance line on status now name that exception. Still to decide moves to section 12. No existing rule id changed.

Rules that scoped themselves by who makes a page or a layout now name the medium instead: a web page built from full-width sections, a social post, an ad, a slide, print or video. Section 3 opens with how to tell such a page from a screen of the product app. The retired colours and the near matches (rule 1.3) are marked as applying everywhere, which rule 1.1 already required. No rule asks for anything new.

The rules now live as data in the design system, the one source for this page, the agent feed and the judge criteria. Added: applied usage per surface, splash files and the generator, no gradients, retired colours. Nothing is left under Still to decide. The minimal splash is two copies of the largest hook, sized as if the icon were 1.15 times the longer side (each hook 0.73 of it), each pinned to its own corner with offsets measured against the longer side, so it works on any aspect ratio. Colours are defined in RGB only. Every button and text link, on any surface, is the design system Button component, except the white primary button on Vivid Pink (rule 6.2), which keeps its own colours, hover and focus outline. No existing rule changed.
Illustrations use Vivid Pink tints; our own illustrations, logos of customers and tools and file-type icons follow the rules; black is 1A1A1A.
Section rule made easy to check: two named kinds of coloured section, a full white section between any two, at most two Vivid Pink, first screen white. "White stays the larger share" removed.
Final: contents list, rules at a glance and click-to-copy colour codes. No rule changed.
Minimal splash zooms against the longer side. Nothing left to decide.
Right splash vertically centred; centre and right zoom against the frame's shorter side.
Tints given as alpha codes. Rules for customer and integration logos, and for purple as a rare playful touch.
